t: Fustat began in 641 as a garrison camp founded by Amr ibn al-As after the capture of Alexandria, and it served as the base for Arab expansion in Africa until Qayrawan was founded in 670.
It grew to about 120,000 people in the 9th century and about 200,000 by 1168, and it was a major centre of Islamic art and ceramics from 975 to 1075.
Shawar, the vizier of the Fatimid caliph, ordered it burned in 1168 to keep it from Amalric of Jerusalem, and the centre of government then moved permanently to nearby Cairo.
dyk: According to al-Maqrizi, the fire that Shawar ordered in 1168, set with 20,000 naphtha pots and 10,000 lighting bombs, burned for 54 days.
ev: Amr ibn al-As founds Fustat after the fall of Alexandria
The Mosque of Amr is built on the site of the commander's tent
The Abbasids take power and move the capital north to al-Askar
Al-Qatta'i is destroyed and the capital returns to Fustat
Gawhar founds Cairo just north of Fustat for the Fatimids
Shawar orders Fustat burned as Amalric's army approaches
Saladin becomes vizier of Egypt and the Ayyubid dynasty begins

f.founded: Founded in 641 by the Rashidun general Amr ibn al-As after the fall of Alexandria in September of that year; according to legend a dove's egg in his tent marked the site.
f.where: On the eastern bank of the Nile, just north of the Roman fortress of Babylon, in what is now the Old Cairo district of Cairo, Egypt.
f.known: The first capital of Egypt under Muslim rule; the Mosque of Amr, the first mosque in Egypt; a base for Arab expansion in Africa; tall residential buildings; pottery and Islamic art; Maimonides; the burning of 1168
f.today: Fustat is a suburb within the Old Cairo district of Cairo, where few buildings remain and the buried remains of the old city are still being excavated.
